requirements.text: 🟡 **LEAN · D1 · Preserve generated attack fixtures and a small historical reader, but do not copy the old application into the new one.**
Keep the attack strategy executable in development tooling, excluded from the CLI/PWA distribution and production imports.
Reproduce legacy decryption through a pinned original revision in an isolated local run when needed; do not retain a production legacy decoder merely for demonstrations.
Keeping only prose would cost less maintenance but would lose the repeatable attack.
- Historical fixtures use generated covers, public test messages/passwords, candidate lists and expected plaintext digests.
Record the generator/attack revision, dependency lock, format/profile, dimensions, fixture hashes and applicable settings.
Keep new-format controls separately.
Fixture randomness may be fixed in test tooling, never by weakening production randomness.
- Preserve the ticket's original observations verbatim as historical evidence.
Mark missing original provenance explicitly.
A recreated run gets its own report; it does not retroactively validate the old timings.
- Preserve the sparse partial-shuffle prefix filter, the seed-alias demonstration, RGB-lowest-bit clearing and envelope mutations.
Store only the minimal historical attack interpretation needed, not a second maintained application.
Normal tests do not require the old runtime.
🟢 **FIRM · D2 · An attack must demonstrate that it understands the format before its negative result is usable.**
Require a known-correct credential to recover the exact fixture message and deliberately wrong candidates to exercise the reader's rejection path.
This costs a format-specific reader and control fixtures; forwarding guesses to the normal decoder alone would miss cheaper attacker paths.
- Distinguish authenticated exact recovery, candidate rejection by a named verifier, inconclusive/budget-exhausted search, unsupported format, and harness error.
Unsupported formats, broken controls and unexpected parser exceptions invalidate the evaluation.
A candidate-derived structural rejection can itself be the cheap verifier and must be reported as such.
- For each supported format/profile/credential mode, inventory recognizable headers, salt alphabets, map/envelope structure, repair checks and authentication.
Record which secrets and public inputs each check needs, where it can reject a guess, and the expensive KDF work actually required.
Public malformed-input rejection is not a password verifier.
- Compare PBKDF2 + HKDF, Argon2id + HKDF and the considered scrypt + HKDF alternative at explicit profiles, plus any selected alternative.
Test the cheapest useful strategy, including pre-extraction/amortized work, rather than assuming every guess runs the whole app.
Report pre-KDF candidate discrimination and KDF invocations alongside time and memory.
Instrumentation alone cannot prove the absence of another shortcut: require format and implementation review.
- Public salts/profiles are not secret root keys.
Authentication checks a candidate-derived key; there is no additional AES keyspace search.
Do not infer password entropy or general cracking time from the fixture dictionary.
🟢 **FIRM · D3 · Keep a behavior catalog that checks exact recovery or safe failure, not today's serialization.**
Use the existing Jest layout for deterministic checks and actual CLI/browser journeys for application evidence.
Replace obsolete envelope/wording assertions rather than repinning them.
This adds cross-platform verification; library round trips alone are cheaper but insufficient.
| Check family | Required cases and expected evidence |

| Exact recovery and capacity | ASCII, multilingual text, non-BMP Unicode, whitespace, compressed/uncompressed and incompressible messages; empty-input behavior as selected; just below/at/above the supported payload limit including format/repair overhead. Accepted inputs recover exactly; unsupported inputs fail without a misleading successful output. |

| Authentication and metadata | Wrong password; missing, four-byte and other shortened tags; changed full-length tag/ciphertext; removed/changed compression setting; changed version, lengths, salt, nonce, profile and credential-mode fields. Run against both platform implementations. An altered protected record must not yield accepted incorrect text. |

| Parsing and resources | Plain images, unsupported format/profile, invalid encodings, truncated records, oversized images/lengths/KDF requests and decompression limits. Enforce the selected bounds before the corresponding expensive allocation/work; no partial unauthenticated text or successful plaintext file. Do not require errors to distinguish wrong passwords from corruption where the format cannot. |

| Placement and seed limits | Keep the historical seeds-separated-by-2^32 example and same-password/dimensions baseline. For the replacement, use its selected algorithm's vectors and check for truncation/aliasing across its key input and required per-image variation. A few unequal maps are not proof of full-strength security; review the derivation and effective seed space. No exhaustive search was previously demonstrated. |

| Damage and repair | RGB-lowest-bit clearing, specified pixel damage, resizing/JPEG cases and damage to initial decoding data. Require exact authenticated recovery for cases inside the later agreed recovery envelope. Outside it, exact recovery is acceptable, otherwise safe failure; never accept incorrect text. Do not invent a survival percentage here. |

| Credential modes | Scope permanent assertions to selected modes. If evaluating two secrets, include separate-stage recognizable-map/envelope guessing, pre-extracted ciphertext, disclosure of either secret, both wrong, wrong-first/right-second, right-first/wrong-second, missing/swapped secrets, altered mode metadata and correlated/reused secrets. Measure independent verifiers; do not multiply search spaces without a reviewed composition preventing independent checks. |

| Real application exchange | Actual CLI encode → browser import/decode and browser encode/download → CLI decode, with exact Unicode and compression recovery plus representative wrong-password/tampered/damaged inputs. Record browser/runtime and artifacts. Node execution of a browser crypto module is supplementary only. Exercise the migration route once that separate decision is settled. |
🟡 **LEAN · D4 · Ordinary tests stay deterministic; attacks and measured evaluations get explicit commands and reports.**
Keep `npm test` as the full unit/integration entry point.
Add development-only commands below during implementation, not now.
Separate runs avoid flaky CI timing thresholds, at the cost of an evidence step outside ordinary tests.
| Proposed interface | Contract |

| `npm run security:attack -- --manifest <path> --report <path>` | Replays a named attack against explicit fixtures and candidate inputs; runs reader controls first; reports outcomes, earliest verifier, operation counts and informational measurements. A completed run is not automatically a security pass. Invalid/incomplete required coverage must be machine-detectable. |

| `npm run security:evaluate -- --manifest <path> --report <path>` | Runs an explicit device-cost, damage or detection protocol, recording the selected kind and all parameters. No benchmark runs as an implicit part of `npm test`. |
Both reports identify commit/lockfile, fixture/corpus hashes, format/profile/mode, environment, workload/seeds, commands, raw results and limitations.
Keep named baseline reports and comparison reports rather than overwriting history.
The release-evidence ticket decides CI wiring, required devices/browsers, review sign-off and artifact publication; this catalog supplies the required checks.
No glossary or ADR change is needed for these tooling contracts.
🟢 **FIRM · D5 · Report detection, image changes, recovery and device cost separately.**
Changed pixels and PNG size describe disturbance, not the probability that an observer detects a hidden message.
A defensible detection experiment costs a documented corpus and held-out evaluation; synthetic covers alone cannot support a natural-image claim.
- Record natural-image provenance, license/redistribution rights and checksums, or a lawful retrieval recipe where images cannot be committed.
Keep synthetic attack fixtures separate from this corpus.
- Split training/tuning and evaluation by source image before deriving resized, compressed or encoded variants.
Do not leak variants across splits.
Fix detector settings/thresholds before the held-out run.
- Compare paired covers and complete encoded images at equal user-message sizes; report encoded bits per pixel, capacity failures, bootstrap and repair overhead, compression and fill settings.
Report payload rates too; do not silently omit covers a candidate cannot encode.
- Publish detection true-positive and false-positive counts/rates at declared thresholds, sample counts and uncertainty, including untouched-cover controls.
Report image-change statistics independently.
Describe which detectors and image population were evaluated; do not claim universal invisibility.
- Damage protocols specify transforms, codec versions, resize settings/JPEG quality, seeds and sample counts; report exact authenticated recovery and safe failures.
Device reports name runtime/hardware, KDF profile, time/memory methodology and repeated-run variation.
Wall-clock results remain informational, never CI pass/fail thresholds or precise user-facing crack-time predictions.
These are proposed original implementation rules, not Stenoxide/HILL code or a validated steganalysis model:
Work on the supported opaque RGB/RGBA8 raster without color conversion or resampling.
For scoring, use `U(p,c) = RGB(p,c) & 254`; never change alpha or upper channel bits.
Use the valid up/down/left/right neighbors of pixel `p`.
Let their count be `d`.
Compute the integer score `S(p) = sum over RGB channels of abs(d * U(p,c) - sum over valid neighbors q of U(q,c))`.
This is a small cross-Laplacian detail measure, not standard HILL.
Its range is 0–3,048; no floating-point or edge padding convention is needed.
Keep at most `floor(pixelCount / 4)` pixels with positive scores, ranked by descending score, then ascending row-major pixel index.
This retains the highest-detail quarter at most; all-flat images supply no eligible pixels.
The 25% choice is an engineering policy, not a measured safe-hiding threshold.
Use the bounded score histogram and row-major tie resolution rather than a full-image comparison sort.
Define the eligible scalar domain in row-major pixel/RGB order over retained pixels, excluding every reserved public-salt position.
The eligible map is public, not an additional secret.
Use the accepted full-strength keyed sampler over this domain, with one continuous stream for header then body, distinct positions and the existing bounded-work rules.
Do not sort by detail for message order or mix in another weak seed.
Group the keyed header positions and then keyed body positions separately into groups of seven.
Number each group's columns 1–7.
The XOR of columns whose current LSB is 1 is the three-bit symbol.
To encode a target symbol, XOR it with the current symbol and flip the one indicated LSB if that difference is nonzero.
Use ordinary LSB replacement so upper bits cannot change.
Extract the three-bit symbols from the encoded groups, never from sender-only information.
Pack each symbol most-significant-bit first.
Zero-pad only the final incomplete symbol of each header/body bitstream to three bits; charge that padding to capacity and require canonical padding when extracting.
Exact authenticated byte lengths come from the bounded framing rules.
These keyed final-group bits are not full-image filler.
The public salt stays raw, outside the matrix encoder.
🟡 **LEAN · D1 · Use the highest-detail quarter as the eligible region.**
Adopt the integer scoring and stable ranking above.
This gives a concrete adaptive rule without a learned classifier, floating-point drift or STC solver.
It spends an image scan and restricts available positions.
The receiver reproduces it from the upper seven bits; it does not need the original image.
Local variation is a heuristic, not proof that an image is a suitable photograph or that a message is concealed.
🟡 **LEAN · D2 · Retain the existing product bounds and calculate the new carrier budget exactly.**

Keep at most 512 stored message bytes after optional size-reducing compression, at most 1 MiB original/decompressed UTF-8 text, opaque noninterlaced RGB/RGBA8 PNG input, at most 1,024 pixels per side/1,048,576 pixels total and 16 MiB source bytes.
Keep the existing cryptographic/parser/worker bounds.
Remove the Stenoxide-specific WASM allocation/build requirements rather than recreate them.
These retained bounds are policy limits, not measured performance or concealment guarantees for our own implementation.
Let `E` be the eligible scalar count after salt exclusions, and `B = min(E, 262144)`.
Retain the conservative stored-bit rate ceiling as an exact integer rule: at most `floor(B / 50)` keyed coded bits.
Do not present that inherited 0.02 ceiling as a validated rate for this new method.
Let `H` and `T` be the complete fixed protected-header and body bit lengths **after** authentication/framing and their respective Reed–Solomon repair, with nonce/profile fields counted once.
Set `G = ceil(H/3) + ceil(T/3)`.
Require both `3*G <= floor(B/50)` and `7*G <= B`.
The reserved raw-salt pool is excluded before calculating `E`; it consumes its own image positions and does not become free capacity.
Separate header/body final-symbol padding and all final shortened-RS blocks count.
Extract only the needed keyed prefix, within the accepted sampler bounds; do not generate or alter unused samples.
Show the actual net capacity and reject insufficient input before output.
No truncation, higher rate, weaker repair or automatic resizing.
The old 655-byte STC ceiling is no longer a codec API limit; any similar arithmetic ceiling comes only from the retained rate/sample policy.
Do not claim that every eligible image admits 512 bytes.
🟡 **LEAN · D3 · Keep the chosen outer repair profile, but make the new mapping limit explicit.**
Retain shortened Reed–Solomon with 16 parity bytes per body block, separate 16-byte header parity and whole-byte round-robin across at most four body codewords.
Retain its licensed existing implementation and final-block rules; matrix coding follows repair and is removed before attempting repair on extraction.
Authenticate before decompression or output.
No decoder retries or alternate modes.
If upper RGB bits or geometry change, the eligible map can change and desynchronize placement.
Salt damage can independently prevent key derivation.
The old STC mild-damage benefit is not evidence of that same benefit here.

Only unchanged encoded files and sample-preserving PNG rewrites within supported parsing limits are promised; other changes get authenticated output if recoverable or the agreed failure, never partial text.
This retains limited repair capability at an overhead cost without promising that repair fixes a changed map.
Keeping only direct unprotected transport would be smaller, but would discard the already selected outer repair behavior.
The existing format/app work incorporates bounded PNG-envelope handling, no identifying public marker/text, safe rendering-metadata handling and removal of personal metadata with explicit limits.
Do not blindly copy ICC/unknown chunks or imply that stripping metadata is invisible.
No full compressor-fingerprint imitation project or imported JPEG-history detector is added.
The existing format/app decisions own the precise metadata policy.
Keep fresh random salt/nonce, separate strong keys, common authentication-failure meaning and input/decompression limits.
Do not copy Stenoxide's image-derived nonce design or other unrelated features.
Recommend unpublished detailed photographs; warn against publishing originals or comparing repeated covers.
Preserve the exported file and an untouched backup.
Existing implementation/release checks must exercise our actual carrier; no new detector programme is required.
The IDs continue the accepted candidate draft: D2 selects its remaining profile; D5.1 supplies bounded-work ceilings; D7.1 carries verification into release.
Its other decisions remain unchanged.
🟡 **LEAN · D2 · Both apps spend 64 MiB and three Argon2id passes on each new password derivation.**
Use **Argon2id v19, memory 65,536 KiB (67,108,864 bytes), time cost 3, parallelism 1, a 16-byte salt, a raw 32-byte root, and empty optional secret and associated data**.
Reserve profile identifier `0x01` for this exact tuple in the new format's profile namespace; the format decision owns its field location and authenticated serialization.
Do not use library defaults or password-hash strings.
This selects measured candidate `a64t3` as a provisional design, not as a proven phone profile.
Compared with the tested 128-MiB candidates, it leaves more memory for images but charges attackers less memory.
Three passes retain more computation than the tested two-pass option.
Neither comparison establishes equivalent attack strength across algorithms.
Native PBKDF2 would remove the added password library but give up tunable memory hardness.
Shared-library scrypt would avoid WASM but change the construction and runtime costs.
Prefer Argon2id because memory-hard processing remains the accepted direction and the bounded experiment supports this candidate's interoperability.
There is no automatic fallback to either alternative.
↳ 🟡 **LEAN · D2.1 · Both apps start from the same measured Sodium packages.**
Use `libsodium-wrappers-sumo@0.8.4` with `libsodium-sumo@0.8.4` explicitly locked.
Pass the raw accepted password bytes to `crypto_pwhash`, set output length 32, `opslimit=3`, `memlimit=67108864`, and select `crypto_pwhash_ALG_ARGON2ID13` explicitly.
Keep native HKDF and AES APIs as agreed.
This avoids introducing another unmeasured KDF adapter.
Its price is the worker/WASM package, CSP and offline-asset handling, notices and dependency review.
Package upgrades require fresh artifact review and matching vectors; the profile identifier describes algorithm parameters, not an npm version.
A load, CSP or allocation failure reports an error rather than changing the algorithm or cost.
The existing exact contract still applies: UTF-8 without normalization or trimming; reject empty input, unpaired surrogates and input above 1,024 UTF-8 bytes.
Each new encoding attempt gets a fresh CSPRNG 16-byte salt and 12-byte GCM nonce.
HKDF-SHA256 uses the raw root, 32 zero salt bytes, and the exact UTF-8 info labels `obscr/keys/1/encryption` and `obscr/keys/1/placement`, without a terminator, for separate 32-byte keys.
AES-256-GCM keeps its 16-byte tag.
Root and child keys stay secret and are never stored in the image.
🟡 **LEAN · D5.1 · Reject work above provisional ceilings instead of attempting an unbounded image or position map.**
For the next complete-format design and measurements, use these **provisional upper bounds, not demonstrated safe device limits**:
- Width and height each at most 4,096; total pixels at most 12,192,768.
This permits the measured photo and its rotation without approving the unmeasured 4096×4096 case.
- Requested positions `k` at most 262,144 and no greater than eligible positions `N`.
This is a position budget, not a promise of message bytes: framing and repair consume capacity too.
- At most `2*k + 1024` 32-bit draws, including rejected draws; absolute maximum 525,312.
Exhaustion fails without biased sampling or a restart.
- Sparse swap state at most `k` entries; no full `N`-entry permutation.
Stream chunks at most 4,096 bytes, with at most 8,192 bytes for their paired input/output buffers.
Preserve unused stream bytes between chunks.
- At most two application-owned full RGBA8 pixel buffers, together at most 97,542,144 bytes at the pixel ceiling.
This does not count decoder, canvas, GPU, WASM or runtime allocations and is not a whole-process memory limit.
- One active derivation/placement operation per app instance.
Reject unsupported profile IDs and any parameters that disagree with the fixed tuple before running the KDF.
Check dimensions and demands before the corresponding app allocations; check draw/state limits while processing.
These limits stay within the largest represented pixel and position counts.
Their price is rejecting larger images or payloads even on capable desktops.
They may need to become smaller after device measurements; they must not grow automatically to make an input work.
JavaScript map entries have no portable byte size, so an entry cap is not a memory measurement.
Retain the agreed AES-256-CTR generator: full 32-byte placement key, all-zero initial 128-bit counter, big-endian counter increment, continuous stream and no wrap.
Retain four-byte little-endian draws, rejection above `floor(2^32/b)*b - 1`, and swap-with-last selection from the canonical eligible domain.
The mathematical `N <= 2^32` bound does not override these operational limits.

[Define the complete protected image format](https://github.com/jdragulanescu/obscr/issues/19) must set bounded source-file, decoding, frame, decompression, bootstrap-search and repair work before that design is complete.
It must also define the eligible domain and reserve bootstrap positions.
Those carrier-dependent limits are not supplied by a KDF workspace number or by this sampler contract.
🟢 **FIRM · D7.1 · Release remains blocked until the completed format demonstrates the claimed cost and device support.**
Carry this selected tuple and these provisional ceilings into [Define the evidence required before release](https://github.com/jdragulanescu/obscr/issues/22).

Require its named physical iPhone/Android and desktop-browser/Node matrix, cold and warm three-second key-ready target, whole-operation memory, responsiveness, cancellation, failure behavior and both real CLI/browser exchange directions.
Record exact devices and versions before their runs; no unnamed device is declared supported here.

Keep the accepted independent-vector plan: root, both child keys, stream and position traces; Unicode boundaries; changed salts; counter/chunk boundaries; rejected draws; unique small-domain selections; altered metadata; wrong passwords; and short-tag rejection.
The experiment's existing vectors are evidence to reuse, not proof of the unfinished parser or app workflows.
Complete dependency/notice review and independent review of the final format and implementation remain required.
The no-shortcut argument is conditional and explicit: public parsing can check structure and resource limits but cannot check a password.
Every password-dependent position or recognizer must descend from the Argon2id root.
Extracted ciphertext still uses the encryption child of that same root.
An inner header, repair condition or GCM tag may reject a guess just after root derivation; do not charge every guess the full legitimate decode time.
Salt discovery must not restore a fast password-derived path.
Remove Mersenne Twister, the public `SECRET_KEY` suffix and obsolete fast-placement callers during production migration, under the separate legacy decision.
Inspect the completed bootstrap and repair design before claiming that no cheaper verifier remains.
Full-width keys remove the deliberate 32-bit seed bottleneck; they do not give a weak password 256 bits of entropy.
Strong suggested passwords still matter, and an old cheaper image can expose a reused password.
This gate costs real-device work and independent review.
Missing access does not waive it.
A failed target returns for an explicit human decision before release; it never authorizes weaker automatic settings.
Let `P = width * height`, and index RGB scalars as `q = 3 * (y * width + x) + c`, with `c = 0,1,2` for R,G,B.
Alpha is never a carrier.
Require `3P >= 128`, in addition to the full capacity check.
For salt bit `i = 0..127`, reserve scalar `q_i = floor(i * 3P / 128)`.
Put bit `7 - (i mod 8)` of salt byte `floor(i/8)` in that scalar's LSB.
These 128 positions are distinct.
Reserve only those positions, whether or not their pixels qualify for the detail region.
There is no larger unused bootstrap pool, salt checksum, repetition, repair, magic or scan.
Read exactly one 16-byte salt at exactly this layout.
The decoder is configured for this single format generation and Argon2id profile `0x01` before reading any hidden bytes.
All profile parameters come from code, never from an untrusted image field.
Check that the implementation supports this fixed configuration before starting.
An image carries its profile identifier only inside the fixed keyed header.
Check it after derivation; it cannot select another KDF or trigger a retry.
This explicitly narrows the earlier requirement to reject image-supplied profile IDs before the KDF.
No such public field exists here.
A future format, old image or plain image may consume one current-profile derivation and then return the common failure.
This effort adds no automatic format negotiation.
A later format change needs its own explicit routing decision.
Use the accepted detail score and ranking exactly: compute from `RGB & 254`; retain at most `floor(P/4)` positive-score pixels, with descending score and row-major ties.
Enumerate their RGB scalars in row-major/RGB order and remove the 128 salt positions where present.
This gives `E` eligible scalars.
Do not truncate that domain to the position budget; the sampler draws across all `E`.
Set `B = min(E,262144)` only for budget calculations.
Run the accepted full-key sampler once.
The first **896 positions** form 128 seven-sample groups and carry the fixed **48-byte repaired header**.
The body starts at the next sampler position, with no restart, duplicate, sorting or gap.
Its groups are separate from the header groups.
A byte's bits and each three-bit symbol are most-significant-bit first.
Zero-pad the last body symbol if needed and reject nonzero extracted padding; no padding is needed for the 48-byte header.
Padding damage can therefore cause failure even if byte repair could otherwise succeed; this follows the accepted canonical-padding rule.
The fixed header is not separately encrypted.
It is stored at secret keyed positions, repaired, and later authenticated as GCM additional data.
It has no integrity status merely because repair or field checks passed.
Its length fields can authorize only the bounded read described below, never decompression or output.
All multibyte integers in this header and in GCM additional data are unsigned **big-endian**.
Header offsets are zero-based.
There are exactly 32 header data bytes:
| Offset | Bytes | Meaning and accepted value |
| 0–11 | 12 | Fresh CSPRNG AES-GCM nonce |
| 12–15 | 4 | Stored message length `S`, 0–512 bytes |
| 16–19 | 4 | Original UTF-8 length `L`, 0–1,048,576 bytes |
| 20 | 1 | Body parity bytes: `0x10` |
| 21 | 1 | Whole-byte round-robin interleave: `0x01` |
| 22 | 1 | Compression: `0x00` raw UTF-8; `0x01` gzip |
| 23 | 1 | New binary format version: `0x01` |
| 24 | 1 | Argon2id profile: `0x01` |
| 25 | 1 | Credential mode: `0x01`, one password |
| 26 | 1 | Accepted adaptive matrix carrier: `0x01` |
| 27–31 | 5 | Reserved, all zero |
For raw text require `L = S`.
For gzip require `0 < S < L`.
Empty text has only the raw representation; accepting an empty wire message does not require the app forms to offer empty-message creation.
Reject every unsupported value, nonzero reserved byte or inconsistent length, without another mode or interpretation.
Keep the accepted exact password bytes, Argon2id tuple and HKDF labels unchanged.
Encrypt the `S` stored bytes once with the accepted encryption child key and the header nonce, using AES-256-GCM with **exactly 16 tag bytes**.
The AEAD body before repair is `ciphertext[S] || tag[16]`.
The nonce occurs only in the header.
Fresh encoding attempts get both a fresh 16-byte salt and a fresh 12-byte nonce; controlled vectors are the only exception.
The exact 56-byte GCM additional data is:
`rawSalt[16] || headerData[32] || width_u32be[4] || height_u32be[4]`.
This authenticates the salt, nonce, both lengths, all settings, version, reserved bytes and geometry.
Header/body partition, salt coordinates, scoring, sampler, matrix rule and RS parameters are fixed by this format/profile, not independently selectable fields.
Do not store root or child keys.
No second encryption or nonce domain is needed.
PNG file bytes, unrelated RGB values, color type, alpha representation and rendering metadata are not GCM additional data.
The guarantee authenticates the recovered message and decoding settings, not the entire cover image or its appearance.
RGB and opaque RGBA encodings of the same samples can interoperate.
PNG rewrites that preserve RGB samples and geometry remain readable if they pass the supported envelope policy.
Retain the pinned licensed ZXing-derived implementation and notices.
The wire code is systematic shortened RS over `GF(256)`, primitive polynomial `0x11d`, primitive element `0x02`, generator base zero, 16 parity bytes.
Equivalently, the generator has roots `alpha^0` through `alpha^15`; data is highest-coefficient first and parity follows data.
Shorten by omitting leading zero data symbols; transmit no zero fill.
Encode the 32 header bytes as one 48-byte codeword.
For the body, split `S+16` bytes into consecutive data blocks of at most **239** bytes.
Append 16 parity bytes to every block, including the last short block.
Do not append an empty block when the length is an exact multiple of 239.
Under the current limit there are one to three body codewords, within the accepted maximum of four.
Interleave body codewords by column: output byte 0 of each codeword in order, then byte 1 of each, continuing through column 254 and skipping a codeword once it is exhausted.
Do not pad a short codeword.
Do not interleave the separate header with the body.
The decoder calculates these exact block lengths, reverses interleaving, and attempts each codeword once.
Use bounded unknown-error correction, no erasure search or retries; reject a reported correction count above eight or a nonzero residual syndrome.
A codeword can miscorrect beyond its radius, so only GCM establishes acceptance.
Let `C = S + 16`, `r = ceil(C/239)`, `D = C + 16r` repaired body bytes, and `G = 128 + ceil(8D/3)` matrix groups.
Require both accepted inequalities:
The 128 raw salt samples are excluded before `E` and are accounted for separately.
The 48-byte header includes its nonce and 16 parity bytes.
Body sizes include the full GCM tag and every parity byte.
Matrix symbol padding also counts.
Compute net capacity as the largest `S` in 0–512 satisfying both inequalities; distinguish no frame capacity from an empty-message-only capacity.
Reject before modifying/exporting the output if the selected stored message does not fit.
| Stored bytes | Body codeword sizes | Keyed coded bits, including symbol padding | Keyed positions | Minimum `B` |
At maximum payload there are 624 keyed coded bytes before matrix packing, plus the separate 16-byte raw salt.
The retained rate ceiling permits 512 stored bytes only when the actual eligible domain is large enough.
It does not promise that every admitted-size PNG has that capacity or that this rate is concealed.
The sender rejects unpaired UTF-16 surrogates rather than substituting replacement characters, encodes exact UTF-8 without normalization, and bounds the original bytes by 1 MiB.
The receiver uses fatal UTF-8 validation and preserves a leading UTF-8 BOM as U+FEFF rather than silently removing it.
No line-ending or text normalization is permitted.
Retain gzip, already used by both apps.
Use it only when requested and strictly smaller than the raw UTF-8 bytes; otherwise store raw bytes if those fit.
An unavailable/failed compressor is an explicit operation error, not that size comparison.
Reject when neither permitted representation fits.
Bound compression output while producing it; a size-bound abort may select raw only when raw fits.
Never encode a partial compressed stream.
For interoperability, use one gzip member with fixed header bytes `1f8b08000000000000ff`: DEFLATE, no flags or optional fields, zero time, XFL zero, OS unspecified.
Its trailer uses standard gzip CRC32 and original-length fields, **little-endian as required by gzip**.
Compressor DEFLATE choices may differ; compressed bytes need not be identical across implementations.
The decoder requires that exact header, a valid CRC/length trailer, one completed member and no trailing bytes or second member.
It must use a bounded decoder that reports complete input consumption.
After GCM succeeds, bound expansion by authenticated `L` and 1 MiB, then require exactly `L` bytes and valid UTF-8.
A final length comparison after unbounded expansion is not sufficient.
Operational ceilings are policy, not measured device support:
- Source and exported PNG: at most 16 MiB each.
Width and height: 1–1,024 each; pixels at most 1,048,576.
- At most two application-owned full RGBA8 buffers, together at most 8,388,608 bytes.
No duplicate canvas raster for codec input.
Preview decoding is separate from raw-sample processing.
- PNG filtered-raster inflation must produce exactly `(width * channels + 1) * height` bytes, at most 4,195,328; check the ceiling while inflating.
At most one such filtered-raster buffer, or bounded row buffers instead.
Reject extra compressed streams, trailing compressed bytes, an early end or excess output.
- Score storage at most one `Uint16` value per pixel (2 MiB), histogram 3,049 counters, eligible indices at most 786,432 `Uint32` values (3 MiB).
A lower-allocation equivalent is allowed.
This is an eligible-domain representation, not a full shuffled permutation.
Keep the accepted sparse sampler, at most `k` swap entries, 4,096-byte stream chunks and at most 8,192 paired stream-buffer bytes.
- Header extraction is fixed at 896 positions.
Before accepting header lengths, enforce the prefix draw ceiling `2*896+1024 = 2816`.
After bounded header parsing, enforce `2*k+1024` cumulatively for the exact total requested `k`; no reset of the draw counter.
This frame needs at most 11,648 positions and 24,320 draws.
The earlier absolute ceilings remain, but cannot authorize a larger frame.
- One salt read, one KDF, one placement stream, one header repair attempt, at most three body repair attempts, and one GCM verification.
Maximum AEAD body 528 bytes; repaired body 576 bytes; total keyed repaired frame 624 bytes.
Repair arrays never exceed 255 symbols per codeword.
Check all sizes before their allocations.
- At most one active operation per app instance.
Expensive work runs in a cancellable worker; cancellation stops it and discards all partial results.
Bounds and cancellation do not constitute a measured wall-clock or whole-process memory guarantee.
KDF/WASM, library, browser, GPU and runtime memory still need the existing device checks.
Both apps read raw samples through the same bounded PNG rules, not canvas color conversion.
Accept only noninterlaced 8-bit truecolor RGB or RGBA with all alpha bytes 255.
Do not resample, convert color, premultiply alpha or alter upper RGB bits.
Check PNG signature, chunk framing and CRCs, IHDR methods/dimensions, valid filter bytes, one contiguous IDAT run, one final IEND, exact raster length and no trailing file bytes.
Reject transparency (`tRNS`), animation chunks and unsupported critical chunks.
Bound total chunks by 4,096 and all non-IDAT/non-IHDR/non-IEND chunk data together by 64 KiB.
Check declared sizes against remaining source bytes before taking slices or allocating.
Do not inflate compressed text or color profiles merely to strip them.
Allow at most one each of `sRGB`, `gAMA` and `cHRM`, before IDAT, with valid standard sizes and values.
Preserve these small rendering chunks byte-for-byte in the output, in `cHRM`, `gAMA`, `sRGB` order when present.
When `sRGB` accompanies `gAMA` or `cHRM`, require their standard sRGB values; reject contradictory declarations.
With no rendering declaration, leave it absent rather than inventing one.
Reject `iCCP`, `cICP`, `mDCV` and `cLLI` instead of dropping color/HDR instructions or silently transforming the image.
Accept and discard these known non-rendering/opaque-image ancillary chunks without expanding embedded data: `tEXt`, `zTXt`, `iTXt`, `eXIf`, `tIME`, `pHYs`, `sBIT`, `bKGD`, `hIST`.
An optional valid truecolor `PLTE` may be ignored and omitted from output; do not use it to quantize pixels.
Enforce their PNG structural ordering/size rules where applicable.
Reject other unknown chunks in this bounded profile rather than copying unknown data or guessing whether removal changes appearance.
This intentionally rejects some otherwise valid PNGs.

Write a fresh PNG with the same dimensions, RGB samples and RGB/RGBA color type, retaining opaque alpha where present, only the allowed rendering metadata, and no identifying comment or application chunk.
PNG filters, IDAT chunk splitting and DEFLATE output need not be byte-identical between conforming encoders.
Never overwrite the original source on failure.
Explain that metadata is removed, that color-managed inputs can be rejected, and that stripped metadata or encoder output may itself be detectable.
Do not claim compressor-fingerprint imitation or hidden-image anonymity.
The only decode route is:
Validate password input and the bounded PNG envelope; obtain the raw raster.
Reproduce eligibility and reject an image too small even for the minimum frame.
Read the raw salt once; derive the fixed Argon2id root and accepted encryption/placement keys once.
Generate the fixed header prefix, matrix-extract 48 bytes, repair once, and check fixed fields and bounded lengths.
These are still untrusted values.
An unsupported field is a rejection, never a routing instruction.
Compute exact body/repair/group sizes and enforce both capacity inequalities before further reads or allocations.
Continue the same sampler and enforce cumulative budgets.
Matrix-extract exactly the body bytes and canonical final padding; reverse interleaving and repair each body codeword once.
Require exactly `S+16` bytes, split exactly 16 bytes as the tag, and verify GCM with the exact AAD.
Only after authentication, decompress if indicated, require the exact original byte length and fatal UTF-8 decoding, then release text.
Native decrypt-update output stays private until final authentication; no preview, log or partial save sees it.
Public PNG/geometry/capacity checks and the raw salt reveal no test of the supplied password.
The salt has no recognition or repair redundancy.
Header RS syndromes, fixed fields, lengths, matrix padding, body RS and the GCM tag can reject a password guess, but each requires positions derived from the expensive Argon2id root.
An attacker can stop at the earliest such rejection; do not charge each guess the full legitimate decode cost.
Direct searches over the placement/encryption keys remain full-width key attacks, not reduced-seed paths.
Extraction of the entire frame does not remove password-based confidentiality.
Weak or reused passwords remain weak; no claim of 256 bits of password entropy follows.
No public format marker is introduced, but fixed salt writes, adaptive selection, repair relationships, metadata changes and PNG encoding can still contribute to detection.
This is an argument about routing and recognizers, not proof of concealment or an independent security review.
Before hidden decoding, missing/invalid password input, unsupported PNGs, resource failures and explicit cancellation can have specific guidance.
After hidden decoding starts, salt/keyed-header/repair/padding/tag failures use the accepted common meaning:
> Could not recover an authenticated message.
The password may be wrong, or the image may be damaged or changed.
Do not identify an unknown hidden profile or plain/legacy image from unauthenticated header bytes.
Authenticated but invalid text/compression also produces no text.
Do not expose internal recognizer-stage diagnostics to users or log secrets.
There is no compatibility fallback, second password, alternate carrier, repair downgrade, retry or recovery promise for changed salt, geometry or upper bits.
The following is a **framing-only test vector**, not an Argon2id vector.
Supply the stated encryption key directly.
Fixed salt/nonce/key values are forbidden in real encoding.
The header becomes one 48-byte RS codeword.
The 18-byte AEAD body becomes one 34-byte codeword.
Its 272 bits need 91 body groups and one zero padding bit; with 128 header groups this is 219 groups, 657 charged bits and 1,533 keyed positions.
Salt positions are separately reserved; no complete PNG fixture is claimed by this vector.

The later specification must retain the accepted independent root/key/stream/position vectors and add complete-format fixtures with salt exclusions, eligibility ties, final-symbol padding, all shortened-block transitions and exact PNG/sample handling.

Required integrated checks still include both real browser/CLI exchange directions, Unicode/BOM, compression limits and malformed streams, altered authenticated fields, full-tag enforcement, plain/old/wrong-password images, resource/cancellation behavior, existing bounded detection and damage checks, named physical devices, dependency/license review and independent review of the finished format and implementation.
This agreement supplies the design; none of those release checks is marked passed by this framing exercise.
No new corpus, detector training or confirmation study is required.
🟡 **LEAN · D1 · The recipient tries one fixed profile and reads only the salt before password processing.**
Use 128 fixed, spread-out raw salt positions and put profile IDs in the keyed header.
This avoids a public profile marker and any salt search.
The price is one derivation even for many plain, old or unsupported hidden images, and unrecoverable salt damage.
Explicitly narrow the earlier pre-KDF image-profile check as stated in the contract.
A public selector would allow earlier dispatch but add recognizable structure.
🟡 **LEAN · D2 · Both apps authenticate one fixed header and one message together.**
Reuse the pilot's clear 32-byte header at keyed positions and one GCM tag, with the exact fields and AAD above.
This avoids another encryption/key/nonce scheme and keeps the frame small.
The price is that header lengths remain untrusted until final authentication; they may authorize only tightly bounded extraction.
Separate header authentication would reject bad metadata earlier but consume additional bytes and protocol machinery.
🟢 **FIRM · D3 · Both apps use the accepted repair rules and charge every overhead byte.**
The contract fixes shortened blocks, interleaving and matrix boundaries without changing the carrier.
The largest stored message uses 11,648 keyed positions and needs at least 249,600 eligible-budget samples.
Its price is limited net capacity and no repair guarantee when salt or placement changes; raising the rate or weakening repair is not an automatic option.
🟡 **LEAN · D4 · Both apps accept exact bounded UTF-8, with one strictly framed gzip member when it saves space.**
Keep the existing compression family, authenticate before expansion, preserve the exact text and reject extra members, trailing data and excess output.
This needs a bounded shared parsing contract rather than each platform's permissive defaults.
Raw-only text would be simpler but would discard the accepted optional-compression route.
🟡 **LEAN · D5 · Both apps reject unsupported PNG color handling and export only approved rendering metadata.**
Keep raw sample values and a small rendering allowlist; remove personal metadata without expanding it.
Fixed file/chunk/raster/worker budgets bound attacker-controlled work.
The cost is rejecting some valid PNGs and possible metadata/encoder fingerprints.
Broad color conversion or blind metadata copying would admit more files but risk changed samples or personal-data leakage.
🟢 **FIRM · D6 · Only complete authenticated text reaches the user; the full release checks still apply.**
Use the single bounded decode path and common failure, without retry or legacy fallback.
Every password-dependent recognizer follows Argon2id, but the earliest one can end an attacker's guess.
The cost is limited error diagnosis and the existing device/interoperability/security work before release; this draft supplies no concealment or damage-survival guarantee.
