🟡 **LEAN · D1 · Put the complete protected-image operation behind one shared module, rather than asking each app to assemble it.**
Create `lib/protected-image.js` as the shared orchestration module.
Retain `lib/steg-core.js` as its carrier implementation; retain the Node/browser adapter locations for real platform differences.
This concentrates security decisions, at the cost of migrating both callers together.
Keeping two full implementations would reduce immediate restructuring but retain drift risk.
The application-facing interface is asynchronous and worker-backed:
| Operation | Input and result |

| `prepareEncode({ pngBytes, message, compress }, control)` | Validates bounded PNG/text inputs and prepares the selected raw/gzip bytes. Returns an opaque preparation handle and `{ originalBytes, storedBytes, compressionUsed, maxStoredBytes, hasFrameCapacity, fits, metadataNotice }`. Runs no KDF and consumes no salt or nonce. |

| `encode({ preparation, password }, control)` | Consumes the current preparation, validates the password, performs one fresh encode and returns complete PNG bytes plus its capacity summary. Does not write a file or download anything. |

| `decode({ pngBytes, password }, control)` | Applies the complete accepted decode contract and returns exact authenticated text, or a safe typed failure. Never returns intermediate plaintext or a partially recovered result. |
| `discard(preparation)` | Releases an unused preparation when its inputs change, the user clears the form or the worker closes. |
`control` carries cancellation and safe progress events, not algorithm/profile overrides.
A preparation is worker-owned, single-use, tied to exact input bytes/text/compression, and limited to one per app instance.
Replacing it releases the old one.
Transfer owned buffers where possible; do not retain another raster or recompress the same prepared text at encode time.
Public file-size limits are checked before reading the entire source into memory, and the shared module enforces its own bounds too.
Preparing and encoding do not overlap.
Platform adapters supply bounded file reads/writes, browser downloads, worker lifecycle, CSPRNG and the agreed native crypto interfaces.
The fixed Sodium implementation and format rules stay common.
PNG admission/metadata, framing, UTF-8, gzip validation, capacity, repair, key/profile settings and safe failure mapping must not be implemented again in either form or command handler.
Low-level compression implementations may differ only within the accepted contract; their outputs need not be byte-identical.
The later migration switches the CLI, browser forms and capacity display together.
Strip framing/compression policy out of the two crypto adapters; remove obsolete exports/callers, dummy-password estimates, `SECRET_KEY`, Mersenne Twister placement, filler and its switch.
Keep no legacy decoder or compatibility alias.
Bring the image-diff flow under the same bounded PNG admission policy; run it separately from a protected-image operation and label it a visual comparison, not a security or recovery test.
Retain necessary licensed crypto/repair implementations and notices, without adding Stenoxide or a full STC solver.
Update README, the next changelog entry, examples and obsolete format tests with the new contract; historical changelog entries remain historical.
🟡 **LEAN · D2 · Suggest six randomly selected words, while keeping user-chosen passwords available.**
Bundle the published EFF Long Wordlist in both distributions, in its published dice-key order, with its source, pinned content digest and applicable notice.
Select six words independently, with replacement, using the platform CSPRNG.
For each unsigned 32-bit draw `x`, reject `x >= 4294964736`; otherwise choose index `x % 7776`.
Join the unchanged lowercase words with one ASCII space.
Do not deduplicate words, impose patterns, use `Math.random`, fetch the list at runtime or fall back when secure randomness is unavailable.
Six words follow EFF's recommendation and limit typing cost.
Eight words would add about 25.85 bits of selection entropy but require two more words to retain and transfer.
The default does not claim the map's 128-bit attack-benchmark strength.
Both interactive apps select “Generate a passphrase” by default.
Generate once for a new encode flow, not on each render or image edit; offer an explicit regenerate action.
Show the exact phrase for recording and require an acknowledgement that it has been retained before encoding.
Do not silently replace an acknowledged phrase.
A user who chooses “Use my own password” enters it twice; both values must match exactly.
Decode asks once, with no confirmation, generation or strength judgement.
Generated phrases need acknowledgement, not a second transcription.
The shared guidance says: “Use a new generated passphrase for each image.
Keep it safely; Obscr cannot reset it.

Someone with the image can try passwords offline.” Detail help may explain the roughly 77.55-bit selection entropy, conditional on unchanged independent generation; it must not translate it into years or promise a lifetime.
For custom or edited passwords, use the same local zxcvbn version and scoring in both apps.
A score below 3 adds “This password may be easy to guess; a generated passphrase is recommended.” Always explain that the estimate cannot establish safety or detect reuse.
Do not show crack times, numeric guess counts or a “safe” badge.
A generated phrase edited by the user loses the generation claim.
Warnings do not block an otherwise valid custom password or add a minimum length/complexity rule; the accepted nonempty, valid Unicode and 1,024-UTF-8-byte limits still apply.
This preserves user choice at the cost of allowing weak passwords after a warning.
🟡 **LEAN · D3 · Make secret entry and output explicit, including in scripts.**
In the browser, allow paste and a deliberate reveal/copy action; never copy a secret automatically.
Disable spell-check and autocorrection on password/message inputs.
Custom-password confirmation and all comparisons preserve whitespace, case and Unicode exactly.

A supported exact UTF-8 message-file input must be available for text whose line endings or BOM cannot be faithfully entered through a textarea; interactive entry uses exactly the text value the control produces.
Both apps reject empty-message creation but accept nonempty whitespace without trimming.
Both can decode a valid empty wire message and show successful recovery even when there is no text to render.
The interactive CLI uses masked password prompts and an in-process multiline message input, not an automatically opened external editor with hidden temporary-file risks.
Users who prefer an editor can prepare a message file explicitly.
Generated phrases are displayed only on the interactive terminal, with a warning about terminal recording/scrollback.
User-triggered browser copy warns that clipboard history or other software can retain secrets; Obscr does not promise clipboard deletion.
For scripts, add `--non-interactive`, `--password-file PATH`, and `--message-file PATH|-`.
Both file inputs contain exact valid UTF-8: no BOM removal, normalization or trailing-newline stripping. `-` is allowed only for message stdin, so it cannot compete with password input.
Do not accept literal passwords in arguments or environment variables.
With no TTY, behave as noninteractive automatically; `--non-interactive` forces that behavior even with a TTY.
Missing required inputs fail rather than prompt.
Noninteractive encoding requires a supplied password and never generates an unrecorded secret.
It shows custom-password guidance on stderr without requiring acknowledgement.
This is a workable script route, but the user must protect any secret files and avoid shell commands that expose their contents in history.
Keep encoded output as a file.
Decrypt uses `--output PATH` or explicit `--stdout`; the latter writes exact UTF-8 bytes, with no added newline, and no banner on stdout.
Without a destination, interactive mode may display safely rendered text; noninteractive mode fails with input guidance.
Browser text renders as text, never HTML.
Interactive terminal display escapes terminal-control characters and clearly says that file/stdout output preserves the original bytes.

All progress, guidance and diagnostics go to stderr; `--quiet` suppresses progress/summaries, not errors or relevant safety warnings. `--verbose` must not expose hidden-recognizer stages, secrets or raw exception dumps.
Exit codes are 0 for success, 1 for failure and 130 for cancellation.
Never overwrite a source or existing output file, including through an alias or symlink.
Ask the user to choose a new path instead of offering in-place replacement.

CLI output is published only after a complete result, using a no-clobber commit and restrictive permissions for app-created files where supported; remove only this operation's temporary output on failure.
Browser downloads begin only after a complete result and an explicit save action.
Warn that a decoded message saved to disk or sent to stdout is plaintext.
This costs an explicit output choice and changes existing overwrite/automatic-download behavior, but protects originals and existing results.
Do not persist passwords, message inputs or recovered text in browser storage, caches, URLs, logs or telemetry.
Clear password/confirmation state and release derived buffers after success, failure or cancellation.
Clear stale results on a new operation or changed inputs; offer an explicit clear action for text/results and revoke discarded object URLs.
Workers release mutable secret buffers where possible.
JavaScript strings, clipboard history, OS paging and a compromised endpoint prevent a secure-erasure guarantee.
No password manager is required and no password recovery is promised.
🟡 **LEAN · D4 · Show message bytes that actually fit, and distinguish input problems from failed recovery.**
Both apps show `storedBytes / maxStoredBytes`, original UTF-8 bytes, and whether compression was actually used.
Capacity includes every accepted header, tag, repair and symbol-padding cost; use the format's exact calculation, not RGB bit count or a dummy encryption.
Distinguish an image with no complete-frame capacity from one that admits only an empty wire message.
The creation form admits neither case for a nonempty message.
Compression stays opt-in.
Use the prepared representation only when the accepted rules permit it and it is smaller.
Show raw fallback when compression does not save space; compressor errors remain errors.
Do not promise “50–90% reduction.” Cap stored text at 512 bytes, original text at 1 MiB, PNG source/output at 16 MiB, and dimensions at 1,024 per side, subject to all stricter format checks.
A detailed image can still have insufficient net capacity.
If it does not fit, suggest a shorter message, optional compression, or a different supported detailed PNG—not an automatic resize, higher rate or weaker repair.

Before encoding, disclose: only the accepted opaque, noninterlaced RGB/RGBA8 PNG profile is supported; personal metadata is removed; only approved rendering metadata is preserved; some otherwise valid PNGs will be rejected.
Report preparation errors instead of leaving a capacity spinner running.
Invalidate stale preparation/results when an input changes.
Use common typed outcomes for invalid input, unsupported PNG, input/resource limit, insufficient capacity, unavailable runtime, cancellation, I/O and failed recovery.
Input/public-envelope problems and local runtime failures can give specific, safe guidance.
Hidden profile/header/repair/padding/tag failures and invalid recovered text/compression all return no text and the settled message:
> Could not recover an authenticated message.
The password may be wrong, or the image may be damaged or changed.
Do not label unauthenticated hidden bytes “unsupported format,” identify an old/plain image, or expose which recognizer failed.
General help explains that old images and plain images can produce the same failure.
State prominently that the new format cannot read old images, with no legacy option, migration tool or old-release recovery journey.
These restrictions reduce diagnostic detail but preserve the agreed failure meaning and clean format break.
🟡 **LEAN · D5 · Show honest operation stages and let the user stop work without weakening protection.**
Use shared progress phases: checking inputs, preparing text/capacity, deriving keys, encoding or recovering, and preparing the result.
Recovery uses one broad stage rather than exposing header/repair/tag success.
Show a spinner and phase, not invented percentages, crack times or a promised completion time.
CLI hides the spinner outside a TTY.
All expensive preparation and encode/decode work runs in a Web Worker or Node worker thread, with one active operation per app instance and all accepted allocation/work bounds.
Browser Cancel and CLI Ctrl-C terminate the operation, discard partial results and suppress late worker responses; cancellation is not an authentication failure.
The next action starts with a fresh worker state.
A changed input cancels obsolete capacity work; it must not silently cancel or restart an encode using a different password.

If required crypto, secure randomness, workers, WASM, CSP permissions or allocation are unavailable, explain that this runtime cannot complete the operation and suggest a release-supported browser or local CLI.
Do not switch KDFs, reduce costs, retry profiles or run an uncancellable main-thread fallback.
Do not add an arbitrary wall-clock timeout: retain user cancellation and the accepted work ceilings.
The three-second key-ready target remains a release measurement, not a timer that changes security settings.
This costs worker lifecycle work; named-device support and complete-process memory remain unproved until the existing release checks pass.
🟡 **LEAN · D6 · Explain local processing, software trust and file delivery as separate requirements.**
Bundle the word list, worker, WASM, codecs and all other required assets with each release.
The PWA caches a complete versioned asset set; a missing asset is an offline-readiness failure, not permission to substitute code or algorithms.
Expose release identity and offline-readiness status.
Stage updates without replacing the running release; activate a complete new set only through an idle user-approved reload, and never combine old and new processing assets.
The CLI ships the equivalent required assets.
This costs cache/update handling, but makes offline operation a checkable promise rather than a claim based only on service-worker registration.
Use this trust statement in both apps and README:
> Obscr processes your image, message and password on this device; it does not upload them.
The hosted app may contact its host to load files or check for updates.
Complete offline use requires the full application to be available locally.
You must trust the application code, its dependencies, its build and update sources, and this device.
A malicious page, update, extension or compromised device can read your secrets.
Working offline does not make code that is already malicious safe.
Do not send secrets to telemetry, external strength checks or external word-list services.
Do not add analytics or third-party runtime scripts.
The hosted delivery risk is a trust assumption, not an observed deployed-site compromise or exfiltration finding.

Document how to obtain a reviewed release, verify available release provenance, install locked dependencies, and run a local CLI or loopback-served production web build offline after obtaining its complete assets.
A local build or same-host checksum alone is not independent proof that code is safe.

Before transfer, explain: send the exported PNG as an unchanged file, not a screenshot or processed photo; keep an untouched encoded-file backup; keep the password separately and share it through a separately trusted confidential channel.
Recommend unpublished detailed covers, and warn that published originals or repeated covers aid comparison.
Repair cannot promise recovery after changed salt, upper bits, resizing or recompression.
Metadata stripping and PNG encoding can themselves leave detectable traces; neither the adaptive carrier nor the diff view proves concealment.
Security help also states that one expensive root plus HKDF supplies separate encryption and placement keys.
A correct password guess supplies the AES key; there is no second independent AES search.
The fixed weakness is the cheaper password-check path, not using one password.
Password reuse can expose several images, including when an older weakly protected image reveals the password.
Authentication establishes neither sender identity nor freshness, does not authenticate every cover pixel, and does not provide anonymity or protect a compromised endpoint.
The later browser/CLI acceptance walkthroughs must exercise this contract:
| Scenario | Required observation |

| CLI encode → browser decode, and browser encode → CLI decode | Exact authenticated text in both directions, raw and compressed; unchanged and supported sample-preserving PNGs. No requirement for byte-identical encoder output. |

| Text and password edges | Unicode, composed/decomposed distinctions, leading BOM, CRLF/trailing newlines, spaces, custom confirmation mismatch, invalid surrogates/UTF-8, empty creation rejection and successful empty-wire decoding; exact file/stdout bytes. |

| Passphrase choices | Six words selected by the common unbiased generator; repeats allowed; explicit regenerate and retained-secret acknowledgement; custom warning without rejection; no generated-strength claim after edits; no RNG fallback. |

| Capacity and PNG handling | Both apps agree on net capacity and all shortened-block transitions; no-frame/empty-only cases, compressed/raw fallback and size-bound failures; supported rendering metadata retained, personal metadata stripped, unsupported color/alpha/chunks rejected without conversion. |

| Hostile or incompatible images | Wrong password, plain/old image, changed authenticated fields, shortened tags, damage, malformed/bomb/trailing gzip and invalid recovered text produce no partial plaintext; hidden failures use the common meaning. Public limits remain specifically reportable. |

| Runtime and cancellation | Worker/WASM/CSP/allocation failures, operation cancellation during preparation/derivation/recovery, input changes and late results leave no output or stale success; no profile fallback or retry. Device cost is measured on the separate release matrix. |

| Output and secret handling | Existing/source files and aliases remain unchanged; failed/cancelled work publishes nothing; stdout is exact and diagnostics stay on stderr; no secrets in URLs, logs or persistent storage; visible terminal/browser text cannot execute control sequences/HTML. |

| Offline and update behavior | Reload and complete both directions with networking disabled after full installation; missing assets fail clearly; a staged update cannot mix versions or replace active work; inspect app network traffic and caches for secret leakage. |
These are future acceptance scenarios, not results of this session.

They feed [Define the evidence required before release](https://github.com/jdragulanescu/obscr/issues/22), including its independent review, dependency/license review, physical-device checks and existing bounded attack/recovery checks.
No new detector programme, legacy support or production work is authorized.
No glossary or ADR text is proposed: the ticket holds the application decision without duplicating settled domain terms or format decisions.
This matrix groups checks; it does not shorten the linked contracts.
The later specification must map each normative clause and each accepted app scenario to a check ID and evidence result.
All rows begin **not run for the completed implementation**.
CI means a required deterministic gate; release means a required evidence/manual gate.
| ID / requirement | Check and required result | Platform | Evidence artifact | Gate |

| A1 — Keys, passwords and positions | Independently sourced root, both HKDF keys, CTR stream and position traces match. Exercise exact password bytes/Unicode and 1,024-byte boundary, empty/missing passwords, changed salts, counter/chunk boundaries, rejected draws, unique selections and draw/state exhaustion. Confirm exact Argon2id tuple, full-width keys, fresh salt/nonce and no fallback. | Node and actual browser crypto/worker paths | Vector provenance, fixtures and results; derivation review | CI + release browser proof |

| A2 — Carrier and complete frame | Verify raw-salt coordinates/exclusions, detail ties and LSB-invariant eligibility, continuous keyed ordering, matrix extraction and final padding. Check the format reference example plus independent complete-image fixtures. Exercise all stored lengths 0–512, shortened-block transitions at 223/224 and 462/463, and both exact capacity inequalities. No output above capacity or changed alpha/upper bits. | Shared engine, CLI and actual browsers | Full-image fixtures, expected text/sample digests and boundary results | CI + release exchange |

| A3 — Authentication and bounded decoding | Mutate salt, nonce, lengths, every settings/version/mode/reserved field, geometry, ciphertext and tag; include missing and all shortened tags. Include plain/old images, wrong passwords, malformed/truncated records and invalid authenticated text. Accept only exact authenticated text; hidden failures give the agreed common meaning. Enforce one fixed profile, one derivation, bounded extraction/repair and one GCM check; no stage diagnostics, partial text or retry. Mutations repaired back to the original may recover that exact original. | Node and browser paths | Mutation/control manifest, results and decode-path review | CI + release negative journeys |

| A4 — Text, gzip and PNG admission | Preserve Unicode, BOM, CRLF, trailing whitespace and normalization distinctions. Reject invalid UTF-8/surrogates, empty creation, invalid gzip members/trailers/trailing data and expansion above bounds; decode valid empty wire messages successfully. Check compression opt-in, smaller-only raw fallback and explicit compressor errors. Exercise PNG size, dimensions, chunks, CRCs, raster inflation, color/alpha and metadata rules at boundaries; retain approved rendering data and strip personal data without conversion. | Node and actual browsers | Exact byte comparisons, hostile fixtures and admission results | CI + release |

| A5 — Shared module and clean cutover | Exercise prepare/encode/decode/discard behavior: preparation performs no KDF/random draw, is single-use and input-bound, and cannot overlap encode. Inspect callers and shipped artifacts: no duplicate format policy, dummy-password capacity, filler, `SECRET_KEY`, Mersenne Twister, obsolete aliases or legacy decoder. Image diff uses bounded admission and makes no security claim. Replace obsolete wording/serialization tests with consumer-visible behavior tests. | Engine, both apps, packed CLI and built PWA | Behavior results, call-site/package review and artifact inventory | CI + release review |

| A6 — Password guidance and exact secret I/O | Verify the pinned EFF list/notice, unbiased six-word generation with replacement, explicit regenerate/retention acknowledgement and no RNG fallback. Check exact custom confirmation, shared warning/scoring, edited-phrase handling and no crack-time/safety claims. Exercise every accepted CLI flag/no-TTY rule, exact file/stdin/stdout bytes, stderr diagnostics, exit codes, masked prompts, safe terminal/text rendering, explicit save/copy and no-clobber including aliases/symlinks. Failure/cancellation publishes nothing; secrets do not persist in logs, URLs, storage or caches. | Interactive and scripted CLI; actual PWA | Walkthrough records, byte/file comparisons, network/storage inspection and regression results | CI where deterministic + release walkthrough |

| A7 — End-to-end exchange and app state | CLI file → browser import/decode and browser explicit download → CLI decode recover exact raw/compressed Unicode, including supported sample-preserving PNG rewrites. Exercise capacity/error guidance, no-frame/empty-only capacity, changed inputs, stale preparation/results and recovery failures. Module calls under Node are not browser evidence. | Each required desktop/phone browser paired with supported Node CLI | Commands/actions, screenshots, non-sensitive input/output hashes and exact recovered bytes | Release |

| A8 — Runtime, memory and cancellation | Exercise maximum admitted dimensions/payloads, low-capacity inputs, all accepted allocation/work bounds, worker transfers and repair with the completed format. Record whole-operation memory and instrumentation limits, not just KDF workspace. Interface stays usable; Cancel/Ctrl-C stops work, suppresses late output and permits a fresh operation. Worker/WASM/CSP/RNG/allocation failures produce safe errors, never weaker or main-thread fallbacks. | Named physical phones, desktop browsers and Node | Resource traces, workload manifest, cancellation/failure observations and raw samples | CI bounds + release device gate |

| A9 — Password cost and alternatives | Measure the selected profile from validated submission until both child keys exist; cold includes library/worker startup. Record cold/warm samples separately. Compare native PBKDF2+HKDF and documented scrypt/Argon2id alternatives at explicit profiles; separate legitimate latency from earliest-verifier attacker cost. Apply D2 below; no published library speed substitutes for this implementation. | Physical iPhone Safari, physical Android Chrome, desktop Safari/Chrome/Firefox and supported Node LTS | Exact hardware/model/RAM where available, OS/runtime, conditions, repeats, commands and raw results | Release; never a wall-clock CI assertion |

| A10 — Repeatable attacks | Recreate the historical prefix-filter/seed-alias controls in development-only tooling. Prove the new-format reader recovers the known message and rejects wrong candidates before evaluating it. Inventory the earliest verifier, KDF invocations, pre-extraction/amortization, placement-key disclosure/direct search, sole-password disclosure and password reuse. A useful pre-KDF password discriminator is a blocker; invalid readers or exhausted searches are not passes. Inspect bootstrap, repair and effective key width independently of instrumentation. | Explicit attack harness against current CLI/browser fixtures | Versioned baseline/comparison reports, candidate lists, public fixture secrets and review | CI deterministic controls + release attack report |

| A11 — Recovery and bounded detection | Rerun existing bounded checks on the actual full format, including raw salt and repair overhead, at equal useful-message sizes and on separate evaluation images from existing lawful material. Freeze existing detector settings before evaluation; report false/true positives, sample counts, limits and capacity failures. Report pixel/size changes separately. Verify supported unchanged/sample-preserving delivery; test RS correction within its symbol radius and damage/LSB-clearing/resize/JPEG outside the promise. Changed salt/map or excess damage may fail safely, never produce accepted incorrect text. No survival percentage or concealment improvement follows automatically. | Explicit evaluation runner; actual new-format images | Existing-data provenance/splits, detector controls, raw counts, damage settings/seeds and authenticated outcomes | Release bounded report and claim review |

| A12 — Offline, updates and distribution | Exercise the built/installed products, not only a development server. Complete offline encode/decode after full installation; missing assets fail clearly. Check version identity/readiness, complete word-list/worker/WASM/codec assets, staged updates and idle user-approved reload; no mixed releases or active-operation replacement. Inspect network/cache behavior for secret leakage and absence of third-party runtime services. | Packed CLI; production PWA in required actual browsers | Artifact hashes, offline/update walkthrough and network/cache record | CI build/package checks + release walkthrough |

| A13 — Dependencies, review and honest documentation | Review exact pinned/bundled crypto, repair and word-list artifacts, transitive dependencies, licenses/notices and upgrade provenance. Independently review the completed format AND implementation. Close findings with evidence or record an explicit appropriate human risk decision; a changed mandatory criterion needs explicit user agreement. README, next CHANGELOG entry, examples and both apps state format incompatibility, unchanged-file transfer, backup/separate password delivery, metadata/detection limits, software/update/device trust, no anonymity/sender-identity/freshness guarantee and no password reset. Keep historical changelog entries historical. | Source, lockfile, shipped CLI/PWA and release docs | Dependency inventory, review with finding dispositions, documentation walkthrough | Release |
All evidence identifies the source commit, lockfile and built artifact hashes, format/profile, fixture hashes, exact environment, command/actions, expected/actual result and limitations.
Reports use only public test secrets.
Each row links its artifact and named verifier; no blank, skipped, unsupported or inconclusive result is silently marked passed.
🟡 **LEAN · D1 · Require deterministic checks on pull requests and a separate evidence gate before either product ships.**
Run the full `npm test`, production build, package checks and bounded attack/vector controls on a declared supported Node LTS in CI.
Keep the accepted explicit `security:attack` and `security:evaluate` report interfaces; benchmarks do not run inside ordinary tests.
Use a protected release approval for both npm publication and public production PWA deployment, tied to the candidate hashes and completed matrix.
A release event alone must not publish an unchecked candidate.
This costs CI/release wiring; tests alone would leave actual browser and device failures unchecked.
🟡 **LEAN · D2 · Measure ten cold and ten warm key-ready runs per required platform, and require every valid sample to meet three seconds.**
Name exact devices/versions before running: at least one physical iPhone with Safari, one physical Android with Chrome, desktop Safari/Chrome/Firefox and one supported Node LTS.
Cold runs reset worker/library state; warm runs retain initialized libraries but derive fresh keys without key caching.
Record workload and thermal/power conditions.
Keep failed runs and outliers; exclude a run only for a documented harness fault, retain it in the report and repeat it.
This is a manual release target, not a CI timing assertion.
It costs repeated measurements and may force a profile/support revision; a median-only rule would hide slow valid runs.
Passing one phone does not establish support for every phone.
Whole-operation memory, responsiveness and failure checks remain separate mandatory gates; no new unsupported process-memory number is invented.
🟢 **FIRM · D3 · Keep existing bounded security evaluations without requiring a better concealment score or rebuilding the cancelled study.**
Require valid attack controls and the existing bounded detection/damage reports on our implementation.
Analyze raw-salt writes, keyed repair recognizers, metadata stripping and encoder fingerprints.
Separate evaluation images from any tuning images using existing lawful material; no new corpus, trained detector or confirmation study is required.
Insufficient statistical power is a reported limit, never proof of improved hiding.
Do not impose a population concealment or damage-percentage promise that the accepted contract expressly withholds.
This keeps the evidence honest at the cost of narrower claims; changed-pixel counts alone remain insufficient.
🟡 **LEAN · D4 · Keep one candidate evidence index and require review by someone other than the implementation author.**
The release acceptance ticket links immutable reports/assets and records pass/fail/unmet per check.

A reviewer with relevant cryptographic and application-security competence examines the full format and implementation, dependencies, attacker verifiers and secret/output paths; an author self-review or automated scan alone does not satisfy independence.
No paid audit is required by this proposal.
Publish the non-sensitive review and finding dispositions.
Fix findings and rerun affected checks, or record explicit human acceptance of a specific residual risk; that cannot silently waive a mandatory criterion.
Code/dependency/build changes require an impact record and renewed affected evidence/review, not a blanket reuse of old results.
This costs review and evidence maintenance but makes release claims traceable.
🟡 **LEAN · D5 · Finish the planning map after agreement, and move possible future failures into explicit release escalation rules.**
Append this decision to the map, and move its two remaining fog notes into Notes as mandatory escalation rules owned by the later acceptance work.
Platform failures or review findings that require a design/support change return to the user before release; missing phone access keeps the gate unmet.
These are future evidence obligations, not known unanswered design questions.
Leave the map open for `/to-spec`; do not start production implementation or close overlapping implementation issues.
This permits specification work now, at the cost of possible later design revision.
Keeping hypothetical findings as fog would leave planning open until work outside this map was already finished.
🟡 **LEAN · D1 · The sender and recipient retain one password, not two.**
Choose route **(a)**.
Explicitly reject both an optional placement password and an optional two-secret decryption mode for this design.
Neither has an established user requirement that justifies its extra handling and loss costs.
**The price: disclosure of the sole password exposes the message.** If protection after disclosure of one separately managed secret is required, route **(c)** is the relevant alternative.
Route **(b)** would instead serve separate extraction and reading roles.
Keep the accepted random-word suggestion and user-chosen alternative.
Users can remember or securely record the password; no password manager is required.
Share it through a separately trusted confidential channel.
Obscr promises no password reset or recovery.
Reusing it can expose several images after one disclosure.
Storing or sending two secrets together would not reliably address that joint-compromise case.
🟡 **LEAN · D2 · Both apps report authentication failure without claiming which password or image component was wrong.**
Use a common failure meaning:
> Could not recover an authenticated message.
The password may be wrong, or the image may be damaged or changed.
This avoids a false diagnosis, but gives less precise help than separate password-stage errors.
Missing or empty passwords can receive input guidance.
Unsupported formats and invalid resource limits can receive separate errors.
Neither app logs passwords or releases unauthenticated plaintext.
With only one credential role, wrong-first, wrong-second, both-wrong, swapped and reused-pair cases do not apply.
The later specification must instead cover:
- Wrong, missing and empty passwords; Unicode handling; repeated passwords across images.
- Malformed or altered mode/profile metadata, with resource limits checked before expensive work.
- Authenticated mode/profile meaning and no cheap password-dependent verifier.
- Rejection of unsupported credential modes without fallback.
- Explicit legacy selection, if supported, and both CLI/browser exchange directions.
These are future acceptance requirements, not claims about today’s code.
**ACCEPTED · D1 · Close the experiment as accepted partial evidence, not as proof of phone support.**
Record its limits here and update the map.
Completed work no longer appears unfinished; the remaining device checks must have an explicit later home.
**ACCEPTED · D1.1 · Let the password-design decision choose a provisional profile, with physical-device checks required before release.**
The later acceptance criteria retain the three-second target, whole-operation memory checks and no weaker fallback.
Someone must eventually obtain real-device evidence through available hardware, a collaborator or a device-testing service.
If the profile fails, revise it before release.
No weaker profile may be selected automatically.

The explicit home for these deferred checks is [Define the evidence required before release](https://github.com/jdragulanescu/obscr/issues/22), which must carry them into the later implementation specification and acceptance ticket.
The password-design ticket remains open to choose its provisional algorithm, exact parameters and limits; this resolution chooses none.
🟡 **LEAN · D3 · Both apps use identical password bytes and derive two secret 32-byte keys from one fresh root.**
Encode the password as UTF-8, without trimming, case conversion or Unicode normalization.
Reject empty input, unpaired UTF-16 surrogates, and passwords longer than 1,024 UTF-8 bytes before derivation.
This preserves the exact password but means visually identical Unicode spellings can differ; the byte limit bounds input handling and must be explained rather than silently truncating.
For each new encoding attempt, generate a fresh 16-byte KDF salt and a fresh 12-byte AES-GCM nonce using the platform CSPRNG.
Retrying encryption starts a new attempt with new randomness.
Public salt is not secret key material.
Derive a raw 32-byte root with the selected KDF; do not store a password-hash verification string or encrypt/store the root in the image.
Proposed exact child-key contract: HKDF-SHA256 extract-and-expand, input key material = raw root, HKDF salt = 32 zero bytes, output = 32 bytes per key.
Info is exactly UTF-8 `obscr/keys/1/encryption` or `obscr/keys/1/placement`, without a trailing zero byte.
These labels name this key-schedule version, not the eventual image-format number.
A changed key schedule requires different labels.
The random password salt and the fixed HKDF extraction salt have different roles.
Keep root and child keys private and ephemeral.
Clear owned byte buffers when practical, release references and never log or persist them; do not claim guaranteed erasure in JavaScript.
Retain AES-256-GCM with a 16-byte tag, authenticate canonical meaning-affecting metadata and release no plaintext before authentication.
The format ticket owns the exact metadata serialization.
HKDF and extra fast hashes do not add password entropy; a correct password guess yields the encryption key without a second AES brute-force search.
🟡 **LEAN · D4 · Use the entire placement key with native AES-256-CTR to generate one reproducible byte stream per image.**
Encrypt zero bytes under the placement key, starting with a 16-byte all-zero counter and incrementing the full counter as a big-endian 128-bit integer.
Web Crypto uses counter length 128; Node must match its bytes.
Consume the stream continuously across chunks, preserve unused bytes, and never wrap or restart it during sampling.
A fixed initial counter is permitted here because each new encoding derives a fresh placement key and has only one placement stream.
Reading the same image intentionally reproduces that stream.
This uses the AES APIs already needed for GCM and avoids binding placement to the eventual password library.
ChaCha20 is also a viable alternative, particularly with Sodium, but would tie this path to an added primitive.
CTR is only the position generator, not the payload cipher.
Any future filler or additional stream needs its own separately specified key/domain, not reuse of this one.
🟡 **LEAN · D5 · Select positions without bias or duplicates, and stop at explicit resource limits.**
The carrier supplies one canonical ordered list of eligible positions with bootstrap positions excluded.
Start a conceptual pool containing indices `0..N-1`.
For each requested position with `b` entries remaining, consume the next four stream bytes as an unsigned little-endian integer `x`.
Let `L = floor(2^32 / b) * b`.
Reject `x >= L`; otherwise choose `j = x % b`, emit pool entry `j`, replace it with the last live entry and shrink the pool.
This is unbiased range reduction under uniform input, not a claim that a finite keyed generator reaches every permutation.
Permit this sampler only for `1 <= N <= 2^32` and payload demand no greater than `N`; zero-demand operations need no draw.
Compute the `2^32` sentinel without 32-bit truncation.
A sparse swap representation may emit only the needed prefix, but must produce exactly the same order as the conceptual pool.
This avoids an unconditional full-image permutation; its peak memory still needs measurement.
The eventual approved profile must also set finite image, payload, allocation and total-draw limits, checked before allocation and enforced during processing.
Exhaustion fails; it must never switch to modulo-only sampling.
The mathematical domain above is not permission to allocate a four-billion-entry image.
Carrier ordering, repair and content-adaptive eligibility remain with their existing decisions; this sampler does not by itself select or prove a hiding method.
🟢 **FIRM · D6 · Permit public structural checks before derivation, but no password-dependent check outside the expensive root.**
The decoder may reject unsupported profiles, malformed lengths or excessive resources before password processing.
Salt and profile retrieval must not require a fast password-derived map.
Every password-dependent position or recognition value must instead descend from the expensive root.
Do not add a separate password-check field.
Retire Mersenne Twister, the public SECRET_KEY suffix and obsolete fast-placement callers during the later production migration; legacy handling remains a separate decision.
The intended cost floor is the selected root calculation, subject to attacker optimizations—not full-image extraction or GCM work for every guess.
An inner header or repair constraint may reject a wrong guess immediately after that root.
GCM authentication still permits offline guessing; strong generated passwords remain necessary.
Independent placement-key attacks must use the full key rather than a reduced seed.
Salt reuse, reused passwords and the weakest accessible old/new image remain attack considerations.
This is a design argument, not proof that an unfinished format has no shortcut.
The complete-format and release decisions must inspect every earlier recognizer, bootstrap/repair structure and extracted-ciphertext path before accepting that claim.
🟡 **LEAN · D7 · Require independent reference vectors for the whole key-to-position chain before fixing the format.**
Record password bytes, salt, KDF profile, root, both child keys, stream prefix, accepted/rejected draws and emitted positions for fixed non-secret inputs.
Compare primitive outputs with an independent implementation or published vectors, then require browser/Node agreement for the composed chain.
Do not use two calls to the same wrapper as independent evidence.

Cover Unicode distinctions and rejected input; repeated password with changed salt; stream chunk boundaries and counter carry; forced rejection draws; one-element and non-power-of-two pools; full-domain uniqueness on small domains; bootstrap exclusions; limit failures; altered metadata; wrong passwords; and shortened GCM tags.
Controlled vectors may use fixed randomness; production encoding may not.
This costs dedicated interoperability work but prevents two apps from agreeing only on ordinary ASCII or short streams.
Later real CLI/browser exchange and security review remain mandatory.
